subject: Natural Language Generation
source_sentence: Natural Language Generation , NLG, is often viewed as a complex process comprising four main tasks : i) macro planning, building an overall text plan; ii) micro planning, selecting referring expressions and appropriate content words; iii) surface realisation, selection of grammatical constructions and linear order; and iv) physical presentation, producing final articulation and layout operations.
title: Towards Generating Text from Discourse Representation Structures

source_sentence: Applying logical inference can play a role in tasks surrounding NLG (e.g., summarisation, question answering, or textual entailment), but also dedicated components of NLG systems, such as generating definite descriptions, which requires checking contextual restrictions.
